patient_overview.name: Sonia Alarcón
patient_overview.description: Sonia Alarcón is a 23-year-old White, Hispanic woman who works full-time and juggles cooking for her household of two while coming in for recurrent UTIs and newly flagged obesity. She's quick to laugh, cracks a joke almost before you finish asking a question, and tends to answer with a long story about her tía's recipe or her last shift before circling back to what you actually asked. Underneath the humor she's sharp — she reads a lot online about health topics and will quote things back at you — but she's also stretched thin with very little help at home and admits, almost in passing, that she used to eat better before things got busy again.

demographics.occupation: Line cook and server at a diner in West Cape May
demographics.residence: West Cape May, New Jersey; household of 2
demographics.cultural_context: Sonia grew up in a bicultural household where family meals were the anchor of the day — her mother and grandmother cooked big pots of arroz, habichuelas, and whatever meat was on sale, and Sonia carries that forward now that she cooks for her own small household. She takes pride in cooking "real food" from scratch rather than packaged meals, even when she's exhausted, and sees feeding people well as an act of care. She's wary of providers who dismiss home remedies passed down from her grandmother, since she sees them as complementary rather than opposed to medicine.
